company.name: Nu Holdings Ltd.
company.does: Nubank is a Brazilian financial technology firm that offers digital banking services in Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. Founded in 2013, it is best known for its credit cards and online savings accounts. However, Nubank has expanded its offerings to cover consumer loans, insurance, investments, and cryptocurrency through its mobile app. Thanks to its success in disrupting Brazil's concentrated and fee-heavy banking sector, the company now serves over 100 million customers across its three core markets. Brazil provides more than 90% of its revenue.

company.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd.
company.does: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. is the world's largest dedicated chip foundry, with about 70% market share in 2025. TSMC was founded in 1987 as a joint venture of Philips, the government of Taiwan, and private investors. It went public in Taiwan in 1994 and as an ADR in the US in 1997. TSMC's scale and high-quality technology allow the firm to generate solid operating margins, even in the highly competitive foundry business. Furthermore, the shift to the fabless business model has created tailwinds for TSMC. The foundry leader has an illustrious base of customers, including Apple, AMD, and Nvidia, that look to apply its cutting-edge process technologies to their semiconductor designs. TSMC employs more than 83,000 people.

company.name: ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation
company.does: ExxonMobil is an integrated oil and gas company that explores for, produces, and refines oil worldwide. In 2025, it produced 3.3 million barrels of liquids and 8.4 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day. At the end of 2025, reserves were 19.3 billion barrels of oil equivalent, 69% of which were liquids. The company is one of the world's largest refiners, with a total global refining capacity of 4.1 million barrels of oil per day, and is one of the world's largest manufacturers of commodity and specialty chemicals.

company.name: Delta Air Lines, Inc.
company.does: Atlanta-based Delta Air Lines is one of the world's largest airlines, with a network of over 300 destinations in more than 50 countries. Delta operates a hub-and-spoke network, gathering and distributing passengers across the globe through its biggest hubs in Atlanta, New York, Salt Lake City, Detroit, Seattle, and Minneapolis-St. Paul. Delta has historically earned most of its international revenue and profits from flying passengers over the Atlantic Ocean.

company.name: RTX Corporation
company.does: RTX is an aerospace and defense manufacturer formed from the merger of United Technologies and Raytheon, with roughly equal exposure across three segments, mostly as a supplier to commercial aerospace and to the defense market: Collins Aerospace, a diversified aerospace supplier; Pratt & Whitney, a commercial and military aircraft engine manufacturer; and Raytheon, a defense prime contractor providing a mix of missiles, missile defense systems, sensors, hardware, and communications technology to the military.

news.title: Can UAL's Q4 Revenue Surge Overcome Rising Fuel and Margin Pressure?
news.summary: United Airlines expects Q4 revenues to grow over 20% year-over-year, building on Q3's 17.4% increase. However, strong top-line growth is offset by high fuel costs (assumed at $4.80/gallon with 2.5-cent EPS sensitivity per cent change) and elevated non-fuel operating expenses, resulting in cautious Q4 adjusted EPS guidance of $0.50-$1.50. Premium and loyalty revenues remain bright spots, but margin compression persists across the airline industry.

news.title: Southwest Q3 Revenue Surges While Fuel Costs Test Margin Momentum
news.summary: Southwest Airlines reported strong Q3 revenues of $8.42 billion (up 21.2%) driven by record unit revenues and higher fares, with average passenger fares climbing 26.9%. However, fuel expenses surged 61.7% to $2.15 billion, creating a $1.08-per-share headwind to adjusted earnings. While adjusted operating margins expanded to 5.4%, the airline's near-term outlook remains pressured by elevated fuel costs projected at $4.55 per gallon for Q4.

news.title: C.H. Robinson Rewards Shareholders With Dividend Increase
news.summary: C.H. Robinson Worldwide increased its quarterly dividend by 1.6% to 64 cents per share, marking over 25 years of uninterrupted dividend payments. The company returned $869.05 million to shareholders in the first nine months of 2026 through dividends and buybacks. Other transportation companies including Ryder System, Delta Air Lines, and Expeditors International also announced significant dividend increases, reflecting strong cash generation and commitment to shareholder value.

news.title: SONY Q2 Earnings Call Highlights Raised Outlook and Gaming Growth
news.summary: Sony raised its fiscal 2026 operating income guidance by 9% to ¥1.87 trillion, driven by stronger gaming and film profits. PlayStation monthly active users grew 7% to 127 million with 4% increase in quarterly playtime. The company is expanding entertainment monetization across gaming, film, and music, though rising memory costs and next-generation console investments pose future profitability challenges.

news.title: PDD Holdings Inc. Sponsored ADR (PDD) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It
news.summary: PDD Holdings has been trending on Zacks.com with shares returning +7.3% over the past month, outperforming the S&P 500's -5.4% decline. The company is expected to post earnings of $2.77 per share for the current quarter (down 6.4% YoY) with fiscal year earnings estimates of $10.64 (+2.7% YoY) and next year at $12.73 (+19.6% YoY). Revenue growth is projected at +14.8% for the current fiscal year and +9.8% for the next. PDD received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting near-term performance in line with the broader market, though it trades at a valuation discount to peers with an A grade on the Value Style Score.

news.title: Should You Buy Nvidia Stock Before Nov. 17?
news.summary: Nvidia stock has declined 15% since early October amid concerns about AI infrastructure spending ROI and competitive pressures, but the article argues it remains a buy at current valuations. With Q3 earnings due Nov. 17, the AI chip maker is trading at 25x earnings despite generating massive revenue growth (106% YoY) and benefiting from expected $1.3 trillion hyperscaler spending in 2027.

news.title: Neighborhood Intelligence (NXH) Reports Q3 Loss, Tops Revenue Estimates
news.summary: Neighborhood Intelligence reported a Q3 loss of $0.28 per share, worse than the consensus estimate of $0.18 loss, representing a -55.56% earnings surprise. However, the company exceeded revenue estimates with $509.31 million, up 98% year-over-year. Despite strong revenue growth, the stock has declined 68.7% year-to-date and carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating due to unfavorable estimate revisions.

news.title: Advanced Micro Devices vs. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing: The AI Sell-Off Is Exposing a Critical Difference Investors Shouldn't Ignore for 2027
news.summary: Following the recent semiconductor sell-off, the article compares AMD and TSMC as AI investment opportunities for 2027. While AMD competes directly in the AI chip market with strong growth (34% revenue increase), TSMC benefits from manufacturing chips for multiple industry leaders with superior profitability (45.1% margin). TSMC is recommended as the better buy due to its lower valuation (23.8x forward P/E vs AMD's 63.0x), stronger financial position, and broader exposure to the AI industry without dependence on a single chip designer.

news.title: Can Chevron's Record Natural Gas Output Strengthen Its LNG Position?
news.summary: Chevron Corporation achieved a new quarterly natural gas production record of over 9 Bcf/d in Q3 2026, driven by strong performance from its Tamar optimization project, Leviathan's third gathering line, and Australia's LNG operations. The company's shares gained 41.3% over the past year, with analyst EPS estimates rising 10.60% for 2026 and 18.14% for 2027. Chevron trades at a forward P/E of 12.92 and holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating with an A VGM Score.

news.title: Prediction: Berkshire Hathaway Stock Tops $700 a Share Before the End of 2030
news.summary: Analyst James Brumley predicts Berkshire Hathaway's Class B shares could reach $700 by end of 2030, representing roughly 30% upside from current prices. The projection is based on the company's strong operating earnings (tracking 17% above prior year), diversified portfolio of blue-chip stocks and cash-generating businesses, and new CEO Greg Abel's capital deployment strategy. Even with conservative assumptions, Berkshire could hold $475 billion in stocks, generate $60 billion in annual operating earnings, and maintain $400 billion in cash, potentially valuing the company at $1.5 trillion.

news.title: Nu Holdings Ltd. (NU) Earnings Expected to Grow: What to Know Ahead of Q3 Release
news.summary: Nu Holdings (NU) is expected to report Q3 2026 earnings of $0.22 per share (up 29.4% YoY) with revenues of $5.7 billion (up 36.6% YoY). However, the consensus EPS estimate has been revised 2.78% lower in the last 30 days, and the stock has a negative Earnings ESP of -5.62%, making it difficult to predict an earnings beat despite a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

news.title: American Express vs. PayPal: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.summary: The article compares American Express and PayPal as investment options for 2027. American Express operates a premium closed-loop payments network with strong margins (13.5% net margin) and high-spending customers, while PayPal offers massive global scale with 439 million active accounts but lower growth (4.3% YoY). Despite PayPal's cheaper valuation (P/E of 11.48 vs. 18.73), the author recommends American Express for 2027, citing its superior 10-year performance and more reliable business model over PayPal's stagnant stock returns.

news.title: Is Invesco RAFI Emerging Markets ETF (PXH) a Strong ETF Right Now?
news.summary: The Invesco RAFI Emerging Markets ETF (PXH) is a smart beta ETF that uses fundamental characteristics to select emerging market stocks. With $1.95 billion in assets, a 0.47% expense ratio, and 396 holdings, it offers diversified exposure but faces competition from cheaper traditional market-cap weighted alternatives like VWO and IEMG.

news.title: Better Foundry Stock: Taiwan Semiconductor vs. Intel
news.summary: TSMC is identified as the superior foundry stock compared to Intel, holding a near-monopoly on advanced chip manufacturing with superior technological expertise, scale, and profitability. Intel's foundry business struggles with customer trust issues, lower yields, and unprofitable operations despite massive capital expenditures, while facing continued market share losses in server CPUs. TSMC trades at a more attractive valuation (17x forward P/E vs. Intel's 32x) and is recommended as the clear choice for foundry stock investment.

news.title: CME vs. Nu: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.summary: CME Group and Nu Holdings represent different investment profiles in the financial sector. CME offers stability with a 62% net margin and fortress balance sheet but modest 6.4% revenue growth, while Nu demonstrates aggressive 43% revenue growth in digital banking across Latin America with an 18.1% net margin. However, the author recommends sitting out this comparison, noting both stocks have underperformed the S&P 500 over the past five years.

news.title: PDD Holdings Inc. Sponsored ADR (PDD) Stock Sinks As Market Gains: What You Should Know
news.summary: PDD Holdings stock declined 1.85% to $80.17, underperforming the broader market gains. Despite a 4.85% monthly gain, the company faces projected earnings decline of 6.42% year-over-year, though revenue is expected to grow 13.35%. The stock trades at a Forward P/E of 7.68, below industry average, and holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with stagnant analyst estimates over the past 30 days.

news.title: GE's Commercial Engines Segment Gains Momentum: Can It Sustain?
news.summary: GE Aerospace's Commercial Engines & Services segment surged 21% to $10.3B in Q3 2026, driven by robust demand for LEAP, GEnx, and GE9X engines. Major deals with IndiGo and Turkish Airlines, along with orders from United Airlines and Delta Air Lines, contributed to a 58% year-over-year jump in segment orders to $15.3B. Services and equipment revenues grew 17% and 38% respectively, with 2026 full-year revenues expected to grow in the low-20% range.

news.title: Wood Mackenzie: Middle East conflict reshapes growth, resilience and partnerships across the region's largest NOCs
news.summary: The Middle East conflict has tested major regional oil and gas companies ADNOC, Saudi Aramco, and QatarEnergy, with mixed outcomes. While Aramco and ADNOC have increased combined operating cash flow by $35 billion through alternative export routes, QatarEnergy faces the greatest challenges with facility damage and production losses. All three NOCs are prioritizing capacity restoration and export resilience, with increased reliance on strategic partnerships and international diversification to navigate the volatile geopolitical environment.

news.title: The Midterms Are Tomorrow. Here's What History Says Defense Stocks Do in the 6 Months After a Midterm -- and the 2 I'd Buy First
news.summary: Despite concerns about a Democratic sweep in the midterms potentially hurting defense stocks, historical data shows defense equities often recover within six months post-election. The article recommends GE Aerospace and RTX as top picks due to their significant commercial aerospace exposure, which provides a buffer against potential cuts to specific military programs. Large defense contractor backlogs tied to readiness, rearmament, and replenishment efforts remain bipartisan priorities.

news.title: Invest in These 3 Sales Growth Stocks Amid AI-Led Market Volatility
news.summary: Despite market headwinds from elevated Treasury yields, inflation, and tariff uncertainties, Element Solutions, RTX Corporation, and Herc Holdings emerge as promising sales growth picks. The article recommends stocks based on strong sales growth, low P/S ratios, positive estimate revisions, solid profitability, and Zacks Rank ratings.

news.title: Buy CVX and XOM Amid Solid Q3 Earnings and Surging Crude Oil Prices
news.summary: Chevron and ExxonMobil both reported strong third-quarter 2026 earnings results, beating consensus estimates as elevated crude oil prices and improved operational performance boosted profitability. Both companies generated substantial free cash flows and reached all-time high stock prices. With attractive valuations below S&P 500 averages and positive earnings estimate revisions, both stocks received Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) ratings.

news.title: Robinhood Markets vs. Nu: Two Fintech Growth Stocks, but One Looks Like a Better Bargain
news.summary: Robinhood Markets and Nu Holdings are both high-growth fintech companies reshaping financial services in their respective markets. While Robinhood generated $4.47B in revenue with a 42.1% profit margin in FY2025, Nu achieved $15.8B in revenue with 18.2% margins across Latin America. Despite Nu's larger scale and stronger growth metrics, Robinhood trades at a premium valuation (47.3x forward P/E) compared to Nu (16.9x forward P/E), making Nu the more attractive investment opportunity for long-term investors seeking better value.

news.title: Prediction: Defense Stocks Like Lockheed Martin, RTX, and Boeing Are Set to Soar
news.summary: Defense contractors Lockheed Martin, RTX, and Boeing are poised for growth as the Department of Defense shifts toward more favorable contract terms. Recent long-term agreements with Lockheed Martin featuring inflation adjustments, cash flow provisions, and recovery mechanisms signal an improved relationship between the government and defense companies, potentially derisk the sector and drive valuation gains.

news.title: Nu Stock Just Cratered, and It's 36% off Its High. Is This a Buying Opportunity?
news.summary: Nu Holdings, a fast-growing Latin American digital bank, dropped 36% from its high following Brazil's election results, despite strong fundamentals. The company continues to expand rapidly with 140 million customers, growing revenue (39-56% YoY), improving profitability, and increasing average revenue per customer. Trading at under 11x forward earnings, analysts view the decline as a buying opportunity given the company's solid growth prospects and market expansion into the U.S.

news.title: Golden Dome Is a $185 Billion Program, but Anduril Is Private. Here Are the 3 Public Companies Building It.
news.summary: The U.S. Golden Dome Initiative, a $185 billion homeland missile defense system designed to protect the continental U.S. from aerial attacks, is being developed by multiple defense contractors. While private company Anduril is involved, three major publicly traded defense firms—Lockheed Martin, RTX Corporation, and Northrop Grumman—are positioned to benefit significantly from this multi-decade program, which could reach $1.2 trillion in long-term sustainment costs over 20 years.

news.title: Nu Holdings Slides After Brazil's Election: Is the Sell-Off Overdone?
news.summary: Nu Holdings' stock fell 20.5% from Oct. 23-29 following Brazil's election results, as investors reassess market risks. Despite strong Q2 2026 operating performance with 39% currency-neutral revenue growth and $1.06 billion net income, credit quality concerns have emerged with 90-day loan delinquencies rising to 6.9%. The company's Brazil-focused business faces headwinds from currency volatility and potential interest rate impacts on lending profitability.

news.title: Chevron Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Refining Margins
news.summary: Chevron Corporation reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted EPS of $5.28, significantly beating consensus estimates, driven by a 185.4% year-over-year surge. The energy supermajor generated $67.8 billion in revenues with upstream earnings rising 72.6% to $5.7 billion and downstream profits climbing to $4.9 billion. Free cash flow surged to $12 billion while total debt declined, and the company announced expansion plans in Venezuela targeting 600,000 barrels per day production by 2031.

news.title: Top Research Reports for Alphabet, ExxonMobil & Toyota Motor
news.summary: Zacks Research Daily features analysis of 16 major stocks on October 27, 2026. Alphabet benefits from AI-led growth but faces rising capital intensity and regulatory risks. ExxonMobil outperforms with strong cash generation from low-cost production. Toyota shows resilience in hybrids despite near-term headwinds. Microcap stocks Waterstone Financial and AXIL Brands present growth opportunities with valuation advantages.

news.title: Investors Heavily Search PDD Holdings Inc. Sponsored ADR (PDD): Here is What You Need to Know
news.summary: PDD Holdings Inc. has attracted significant investor interest lately. The stock returned +1.9% over the past month, outperforming the S&P 500's -1.2% decline. While revenue growth is projected at +14.8% for the current fiscal year, earnings per share are expected to decline -6.4% in the current quarter. The company holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with a Grade A valuation score, suggesting it trades at a discount to peers but may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.title: Why the Market Dipped But PDD Holdings Inc. Sponsored ADR (PDD) Gained Today
news.summary: PDD Holdings Inc. gained 1.29% on October 13, 2026, outperforming a broader market decline. The stock closed at $81.96 with a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating. While quarterly EPS is expected to decline 6.42% year-over-year, revenue is projected to grow 13.35%. PDD trades at a Forward P/E of 7.6, below the industry average of 15.29, and has a PEG ratio of 0.6, suggesting potential value.

content.thinking:
I'm noting that oil is elevated because of the Middle East conflict, with XOM at an all-time high and jet fuel around $4.80 a gallon, and that QatarEnergy's facility was damaged. I'm also checking the Brazil runoff from October 25, where NU fell about 36% from its high, and I suspect the market reaction was negative.

I'm checking whether Lula actually won the Brazil runoff, since that would explain the negative market reaction. I'm also watching the midterms on November 3, where a Democratic sweep could weigh on defense names. Semis are selling off ahead of Nvidia's November 17 earnings, the S&P is down about 5.4% over the past month, and Treasury yields, inflation, and tariffs are all adding pressure. Next I'll look at how exposed the portfolio is to these.

I'm listing the channels I want to add: oil via USO, semis via SMH or SOXX, Brazil with EWZ, China and EM with FXI, Taiwan with EWT, defense with ITA, rates with TLT or IEF, the dollar with UUP, and airlines with JETS. Next I'll look up what's happening in the world, running several searches at once.

result.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between the United States and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between the United States and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian policies, obligations, or commitments  aimed at permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and December 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for December 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after the date on which such data is first released to allow for corrections. Data integrity issues refer only to clerical or other similar errors in the underlying data, and do not include cases where IMF Portwatch differs from alternative sources.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

Brazil's rate path, with BCB hikes priced for January and March 2027, also bears on NU, so I'll look at it next.

I'm checking how oil moved when Hormuz reopened in April and again in July, since that gives a basis for the consequences of an Iran deal. Goldman's and others' forecasts are next. The deal event itself looks like roughly a 35% chance by May 2027.

I'm weighing the Iran situation next: the Israel–Iran ceasefire is priced at roughly a 54% chance of breaking down by December 31, which would push oil up and hit risk assets, while the Hormuz deal and a ceasefire collapse aren't mutually exclusive. I'm settling on the Israel–Iran ceasefire breakdown as the second event, since its market can be read directly: about 68% once the chance of it happening between January and May is added to the December figure. A single strike might not move markets much, though a full return to war would, so the estimate averages over the different ways the event could occur.

passages.under: Why is Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing stock plunging today?
passages.passage: Investing.com -- Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ADR fell 9.8% in morning trading to reach $357.16, as a sweeping Democratic victory in the November 4 U.S. midterm elections sent shockwaves through the AI and semiconductor sector, with investors rapidly repricing the regulatory risk surrounding data center construction and AI infrastructure spending across the United States.

passages.under: Why is Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing stock plunging today?
passages.passage: The primary catalyst was the Democratic Party’s capture of both chambers of Congress and key governorships in Texas and Georgia — two states that together account for roughly a third of all planned AI data center investment in the country. Analysts at Evercore ISI warned that "a more restrictive data center development environment could create incrementally more negative sentiment for AI infrastructure exposed names," while Wedbush’s Dan Ives called the Texas result the "biggest worry" for technology investors on election night. Since TSMC is the world’s dominant manufacturer of advanced chips powering AI data centers, any threat to the pace of that buildout flows directly to its order book and growth outlook. Adding to the pressure, investors are also growing cautious ahead of TSMC’s November 10 monthly sales report, which must clear a demanding $53.3 billion quarterly revenue hurdle to justify the stock’s elevated valuation. Bernstein’s same-day price target raise to $600, citing surging custom ASIC CPU demand from Amazon and Google, was unable to counteract the wave of institutional selling.

passages.under: Key Elements
passages.passage: After the results of the U.S. midterm elections emerged, concerns that regulation of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers would tighten rapidly intensified, U.S. tech stocks were the first to crater, and selling pressure spread across Asia on Friday (the 6th). Taiwan stocks opened with a gap down, breaking below the 40,000-point psychological threshold and the annual moving average, hitting an intraday low of 37,837.05 points—a plunge of 3,737.67 points that set a new record for the largest intraday point drop in Taiwan stock market history, with more than 500 listed and OTC companies hitting limit-down at one point.

passages.under: Key Elements
passages.passage: The source of this storm was in Washington. The Democratic Party won a landslide victory in the midterm elections, and markets feared that future review of new AI data center construction would slow and regulations would tighten, directly hitting the order visibility of Taiwan's AI supply chain. All four major U.S. stock indices fell sharply on the 5th: the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,709.67 points, or 3.2%; the Nasdaq plunged 5.03%; and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index cratered 12.25%, with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing's ADR also tumbling more than 10%. Asian stock markets opened broadly lower, with South Korean stocks plunging more than 8% in early trading and triggering a circuit breaker, while Japanese stocks also fell more than 7%.

passages.under: What a Recession Looks Like
passages.passage: As the chart shows, recessions come side-by-side with stock market losses. Of the 11 recessions since 1950, the average recession ends after 312 days and with the stock market down only 1%. The average market bottom during the recession comes after 169 days with the S&P500 down 21%. These summary statistics are superimposed on the chart, below.

passages.under: What About After?
passages.passage: As shown above, by the time the average recession has ended the stock market has fully recovered. What happens next? Do markets tend to over-perform in the period right after a recession? This should be pretty easy to observe over the last 70 years.

passages.under: What About After?
passages.passage: To better visualize this, the below chart shows the same data, but indexed to begin at the end of the average recession calculated in the section above.

passages.under: What About After?
passages.passage: Now it is quite clear that in every recession except 2001, the 1-year period after the recession formally ended produced positive S&P500 returns. In fact, the average S&P500 return in the 1-year period after a recession ended was +15.5%. This is illustrated as another dotted line below.

passages.under: What Came Before?
passages.passage: The year before each recession seems pretty well distributed. Once again, graphing the average performance (dotted line) shows that on average the S&P500 falls about 4% in the each prior to each recession.

passages.under: Conclusion
passages.passage: - In the year prior to each recession, the market drops only 4%, with much more downside to come. - The recession itself sees steep market sell-offs, shedding ~20% of value in less than 6-months. - Recovery from the market bottom is swift and severe. The average recovery is almost +40% in the ~18months following the market bottom in the midst of the recession.

I'm checking the Israel–Iran strike event, where the proposition is direct strikes resuming by May 5, 2027, and the market on the ceasefire holding through December 31 sits at 0.46. Under the complement, the proposition that either side strikes the other by year-end ends the ceasefire, and that would imply the strike event.

I'm weighing whether the ceasefire market's start date matters for the strike criteria, since the earlier market creation dates would have resolved a strike that happened before now. Since the Dec 31 market is still open at 0.46, no qualifying strike has happened yet, so the strike proposition can be phrased as occurring between now and Dec 31, 2026.

I'm estimating the chance of strikes resuming by May 2027 as roughly 0.68, assuming a quiet December gives about a 30% chance of strikes in the following months. For the consequences, I'm weighing a limited exchange, which might barely move oil, against a full-scale war that pushed prices up sharply earlier in 2026. With Hormuz already effectively closed, a resumption probably mostly adds a risk premium, and I'm sizing the implied moves in USO, SPY and ITA from the October level against where prices are now.

input.text: Basis for prop:3, Israel and Iran resuming strikes. Probability: Polymarket prices the Israel–Iran ceasefire holding through Dec 31 at 0.46 (market:polymarket:3399468), so a break by year-end is 0.54. The same series has it holding through Nov 30 at 0.62 and through Dec 15 at 0.52, a hazard of roughly 10–20% a month right now. Netanyahu is pressing for a post-midterm air campaign, and Trump has not decided (src:4). For the case of no strike through Dec 31 I state P = 0.30 for Jan 1–May 5, 2027: a quiet December would mean the talks had held, so I use a lower hazard of ~8% a month over 4.2 months. The point is 0.54 + 0.46 × 0.30 ≈ 0.68. Consequences (link:24, link:25, link:26) are gaps at May 5, averaged over everything from a one-off exchange to a renewed air war. Oil, USO +18 (+12%): the full war start in Feb–Mar 2026 lifted USO 60% (cmp:57), but Hormuz traffic is already mostly cut and the market already carries a large premium. The best guide to the extra premium a resumption adds is the move from Oct 30 (168.83) to now (148.41, cmp:59), +14%, which I shade to +12% because some outcomes are a single limited strike. S&P 500 −18.4 (−2.5%): SPY fell 3.1% in the first month of the war (cmp:57), and a resumption is less of a surprise. Defense, ITA +2.07 (+3% raw): defense stocks gained relative to the market during escalations (ITA's residual was +2.7% in Feb–Mar 2026, cmp:57).

result.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of the Republic of China (Taiwan) by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Territory under the administration of the Republic of China, including any inhabited islands, will qualify; however, uninhabited islands will not qualify.

result.question: Will China blockade Taiwan in 2026?
result.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China (People's Republic of China) announces it has established or otherwise de facto establishes an aerial or naval blockade for the territory of Taiwan (Republic of China) by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying blockade is:
- Prevents the normal ingress or egress of foreign commercial traffic to or from Taiwan Island’s main ports or airports by threat or use of force for ≥ 24 hours.
- Covers part or whole of the main island of Taiwan (Formosa).
- Is declared and enforced, de facto (e.g., it is established that China is blocking a significant portion of foreign commercial traffic, as described above, by a wide consensus of credible reporting regardless of whether China has issued a statement or not), or China-issued navigation/airspace prohibitions covering Taiwan's main island's approach lanes that are actively enforced so that most foreign commercial access is denied.

A qualifying blockade is not:
- Military or naval exercises or drills (established with warning areas or NOTAMs that do not actively stop third-country ships/aircraft and do not materially deny access).
- Purely economic or coercive measures (e.g., sanctions, customs delays, fishing bans, cyber/GPS jamming) without physical interdiction or enforced closure).
- Weather/accident-related closures or voluntary rerouting by operators absent PRC enforcement.
- Islet-only incidents that do not involve the main island of Taiwan.
- Seizure or inspection of a single vessel/aircraft by itself, unless part of an enforced pattern that denies access as defined above.

The resolution source for this market will be a broad consensus of credible reporting.

For prop:10 (invasion by May 5, 2027), I take P = 0.70 that an invasion falling between Jan 1 and Jun 30, 2027 comes by May 5. May 5 is 125 of those 181 days (0.69), and the April crossing-weather window falls inside it. That gives ≈ 0.044. A blockade without an invasion adds P = 0.02 over the horizon. Polymarket's own 2026 blockade market is 0.023 for eight weeks (market:polymarket:2382819), but its book is only ~$90 deep and long-shot contracts sit above belief, and there has been no blockade of Taiwan in 75 years. The point is ≈ 0.063. Consequences (link:49, link:51–55), gaps at May 5, weighting invasion about 70% and blockade 30%. Bloomberg Economics puts a US–China war over Taiwan at ~$10.6T, 9.6% of world GDP, worse than Covid or the 2007–09 crisis (src:11), and a blockade at roughly half that (src:12). In the GFC the S&P fell 57%, and the average recession trough is −21% (src:10). I take S&P 500 −17% (−125) as a weighted average, since the window ends within months of the shock. Semiconductors (SMH) −35% raw (−163), since TSMC makes most advanced chips. Taiwan stocks (EWT) −45% raw (−40.2), since Bloomberg's modeling has Taiwan's GDP down ~40% in a war. China stocks (FXI) −30% raw (−10.5), from sanctions. TSMC's own ADR −60% (−227) under seizure or blockade risk to its fabs. Defense (ITA) −5% raw (−3.45), which is about +8% relative to the market.

Q3 2026 GDP grew at 3.4% (src:13) and October payrolls beat forecasts, so the only qualifying pair inside the horizon is Q4 2026 plus Q1 2027, with Q1's advance estimate due in late April. That is one of four remaining consecutive-quarter pairs through Q4 2027, and with the economy still strong now, later pairs are more likely. NBER announcements typically lag by 6–12 months. I therefore put P(recession visible by May 5 | recession by end-2027) at 0.15, below the 0.25 an even split across the four pairs would give. The point is 0.315 × 0.15 ≈ 0.047. Consequences (link:68, link:70, link:71), gaps at May 5. S&P 500 −147 (−20%): in the 11 recessions since 1950 the market bottomed about 169 days in, down 21% on average (src:10). Oil, USO −29.7 (−20%), from demand destruction. That is smaller than the 2008 or 2020 collapses, because the supply shock from Hormuz cushions the fall. Long Treasuries, TLT +4.9 (+6%): falling yields as the Fed reverses course; with a 10-year near 5%, a 50–75bp fall is about +6% on TLT. Semis, Taiwan, airlines and Brazil follow their fitted coefficients on the market.

result.question: Will the Fed increase interest rates by 25 bps after the December 2026 meeting?
result.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's December 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for December 8-9, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their December meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

result.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the State of Texas enacts a law or constitutional provision that establishes a statewide moratorium on new data centers between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A statewide moratorium on new data centers refers to a binding policy with legal force that generally prohibits or suspends the approval, permitting, construction, grid interconnection, or operation of all new data centers, or a subset of data centers that includes all new data centers with an interconnection capacity above 100 MW per facility (requested or nameplate), throughout the state. Suspensions of tax incentives, exemption certifications, or economic development awards alone will not qualify, nor will a moratorium adopted by a local government or limited to part of the state. Specific exemptions (e.g., for specified applications, executed agreements, or interconnection requests) do not prevent a measure from generally applying to all new data centers, or a qualifying subset of new data centers, provided that data center approval, permitting, construction, grid interconnection, or operation is prohibited by default, rather than permitted subject to conditions or restrictions. Conditions on the resumption or termination of a suspension do not make a measure one that permits subject to conditions; a measure that suspends approvals, permitting, construction, or interconnection until a specified condition is satisfied qualifies.

Enactment occurs when a bill becomes law under the state's constitution and laws, whether by gubernatorial signature, veto override, becoming law without signature, approval at a statewide referendum election, or any other legal mechanism by which statutes can be enacted. For an initiated or referred statute or constitutional amendment, or other voter referendum, the relevant law is considered to have been enacted on the election day on which it was approved, as reflected in the certified results, regardless of when the measure is certified or takes effect. Passage by one or both chambers, or a Governor's announced intent to sign, is not enactment.

Executive orders, agency orders, and other measures which are not statutory or constitutional do not qualify as enactment regardless of legal force. A provision removed by line-item veto is not enacted unless the veto is overridden as to that item. The operative text of the measure at enactment controls; provisions amended out before enactment do not qualify.

The moratorium provision must be mandatory on its face. A statute that merely authorizes a state agency or the Governor to impose a moratorium at their discretion does not qualify. A statute that directs suspension of approvals or interconnection upon a specified condition qualifies only if the condition is objectively determinable and is not deferred to be determined by the implementing agency's findings, certifications, or completion of its own proceedings.

This market resolves based on the date of enactment, not the effective date. Resolution will not be affected by failure to implement a law, judicial invalidation, repeal, or expiry that follows a relevant enactment, or an effective date that comes after the date of enactment.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the state government of Texas; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market will resolve according to the general tariff rate on imports into the United States from the People's Republic of China on December 31, 2026, 12:00 PM ET.

The general tariff rate refers to the base tariff rate paid on imports, including any general tariff the U.S. imposes on all imports (e.g. a 10% tariff on all U.S. imports and a 10% tariff on top of that on Chinese imports would equal a 20% tariff).

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Item specific exceptions or increases will not be considered (i.e. this market does not refer to the effective tariff rate).

Only tariffs which are in effect will qualify. Tariffs which are paused, or which have been announced but have not yet gone into effect will not be considered.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible information will also be used.

This market will resolve according to the change in basis points in the target for the Selic rate resulting from the March 2027 meeting of the Bank of Brazil’s Monetary Policy Committee (COPOM), relative to the level it was prior to this meeting.

The resolution source will be official information from the Bank of Brazil, including the statement or release from its March 2027 Monetary Policy Committee meeting, scheduled for March 16 and March 17, 2027, as listed on the official Bank of Brazil calendar (https://www.bcb.gov.br/en/about/bcb-calendar?categoria=Monetary%20Policy%20Committee%20(Copom)). This market may resolve as soon as the statement or release of the Bank of Brazil's March 2027 Monetary Policy Committee meeting with relevant data is issued. 

If the specified rate is defined by an upper and lower bound, the relevant change will be the change to the upper bound.

If the specified rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded according to the following guidelines. Increases or decreases of less than 25 bps will be rounded to 25 bps (e.g. an increase or decrease of 10 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 25 bps). Increases or decreases of greater than 25 bps will be rounded to the nearest 25 bps and will be rounded away from 0 in cases of equidistance (e.g., an increase or decrease of 37.5 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 50 bps). input.text: Basis for prop:21, Brazil's central bank resuming hikes by the March 17, 2027 Copom. Probability: Copom held the Selic at 13.75% on Nov 5, ending five straight cuts after the market turmoil that followed Lula's Oct 25 win (src:6). Economists expect the rate to stay there until late 2027 (src:6), and Lula is deferring fiscal decisions until after a trip that ends Nov 15. Polymarket prices a March 2027 hike at 0.175 for +25bp (market:polymarket:6404265) and 0.145 for +50bp or more (market:polymarket:6404266), an exclusive 0.32 for any March hike. The books are thin ($30–40 deep), so the interval is wide. A hike in December (0.028 across brackets) or January (~0.22: market:polymarket:6404214, market:polymarket:6404215) usually starts a cycle that continues into March. I put the chance of a Dec or Jan hike with no March hike at ~0.05, which makes P(event | no March hike) ≈ 0.08. The point is 0.32 + 0.68 × 0.08 ≈ 0.37. Consequences (link:118, link:119), gaps at May 5. Brazil stocks, EWZ −2.56 (−8% raw): resumed hikes would mean the fiscal fears were confirmed. Lula's win itself sent the Ibovespa down 13.9% in a day and EWZ 23% in a month (its largest month, Oct 5–Nov 3, 2026). A hike is a smaller, partly anticipated version of that shock. Nu Holdings, NU −1.44 (−12% total): NU fell 16.95% the day after the election (src:17). Higher Selic raises Nubank's funding costs and pressures credit quality, with 90-day delinquencies already at 6.9%, so I take more than its EWZ beta gives, about 4.5% beyond it.

result.question: Government shutdown by December 31?
result.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government enters a shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A U.S. federal government shutdown is considered to have gone into effect when there is a lapse in appropriations that results in federal government agencies suspending non-excepted operations, typically including the furlough of non-excepted federal employees.

A lapse in appropriations occurs when Congress fails to enact, or the President fails to sign into law, legislation providing funding authority for federal government operations by an applicable deadline, resulting in a funding lapse. A lapse in appropriations where no federal agencies cease or suspend non-excepted operations will not qualify as a shutdown.

Partial shutdowns qualify. A shutdown affecting one or more, but not all, federal agencies constitutes a shutdown.

The following will qualify as a shutdown:

- An official directive from the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) ordering heads of affected agencies to execute shutdown plans (e.g., an instruction to "execute plans for an orderly shutdown") that is in effect by the specified date and time
- An official operating status published by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) indicating that, due to a lapse in appropriations, federal government operations are suspended, reduced, or vary by agency (e.g., a notice that "due to a partial lapse in appropriations, Federal Government operations vary by agency")

The following will not qualify as a shutdown:

- A technical lapse in appropriations where OMB or other authorized authority directs agencies to continue normal or substantially normal operations
- Government closures or operating status changes resulting solely from Federal holidays, inclement weather, natural disasters, or other emergencies, unless such closures coincide with a qualifying shutdown caused by a lapse in appropriations

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the United States government, including the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

content.thinking:
I'm weighing whether a shutdown by the end of 2027 is more likely than one by May 2027, since a December deadline could roll a stopgap into early 2027 with another cliff nearby. A Democratic Congress from January 3 against Trump adds to that risk, and I'm setting the chance of no shutdowns at all through 2027 at about 0.17 to work out the probability of at least one.

I'm working out the chance of at least one shutdown by the end of 2027 as 0.83, then averaging in the odds of a shutdown in the remaining stretch if none happens by December 31, which I'm putting at roughly 0.35. That gives a combined estimate of about 0.60, and the consequences look small enough that I'll include it.

content.text:
I've put 10 events in the ledger. Two things about the portfolio explain most of the results:

- **It moves almost one-for-one with the S&P 500.** Its sensitivity to the index is about 1.03, so most events reach you through the broad market.
- **XOM and DAL roughly cancel each other on oil.** When oil rises, Exxon gains about what Delta loses, so your net oil exposure is close to zero. The Iran events hurt or help you mainly through the stock market and defense stocks, not through oil itself.

The biggest single concentration is Taiwan. TSM ($35k) plus the Taiwan-listed part of EEM (about 26% of the fund) comes to roughly $48k, about a quarter of the portfolio. Most of it is chipmakers.

Two recent shocks frame this:
- **Brazil:** Lula's runoff win on Oct 25 knocked NU down 17% in one day.
- **Chips:** on Nov 5 the chip index fell 12% in one day. The Democrats won both houses of Congress and the Texas and Georgia governorships, and markets fear limits on new AI data centers.

**What stands out**
- **Taiwan is the worst case.** If China invades or blockades Taiwan, I estimate TSM's own shares fall about 60% (−$21k) and EEM loses about $15k.
- **A US recession is the other big loss.** It is unlikely to show up in the data before May, but it would hit TSM, DAL, NU and EEM together.
- **The Iran events point in different directions.** A US–Iran deal to reopen Hormuz is more likely than not and helps you on balance: DAL, EEM, TSM and NU gain, XOM and RTX give some back. Renewed Israel–Iran strikes or a US ground offensive cost you a few thousand each, with RTX partly offsetting.
- **NU's main risk is Brazil's central bank raising rates again.** That would confirm the fiscal fears from the election. NU accounts for about $3.6k of that event's $4.3k full impact.

**Where the numbers rest on my own judgment**
- **Probabilities:** most come from Polymarket prices, but I had to extend them to May 5. For example, the 0.35 chance of a Hormuz deal in January–May if none comes by year-end, and the 0.15 chance that a recession shows up in the data by May. The US–China tariff probability (10%) is entirely my own estimate, because those markets are too thin to trust.
- **The Brazil probability (37%) is soft too.** It rests on markets only $30–40 deep.
- **How much each event moves prices** is my estimate from past episodes and published research. The note on each event shows the source behind each figure.

**Not in the ledger:** Nvidia's results on Nov 18, TSMC's monthly sales report on Nov 10, Lula's fiscal speech on Nov 8, and the new Congress's fight over the defense budget. I left out the first three because no clean, tradeable event defines them, and the defense budget because I didn't build it out. I can add any of them if you want.
